newsitem.title: UK: Dry cargo freight rates ease again.
newsitem.headline: Dry cargo freight rates ease again.

text.p: The Baltic Freight Index (BFI) fell again on Wednesday, off six to a new post-1992 low of 1,045 points, reflecting continued weakness in most sectors of the dry cargo freight market.
The focus was on easier, sub-$19 fixtures for Panamaxes in the thin nearby grains trade.
Reported fixtures included Continental for Hanjin tonnage 54,000/5 heavy grains US Gulf/Japan for 18-23 September at $18.75 with no combination.
Pateras was reported fixed 55,000/5 tonnes heavy grain US Gulf/Taiwan at $18.75 for 10-14 September to charterers for the account of Continental.
Brokers continue to say available tonnage is weighing on the dry cargo freight market through to November with the prospect that U.S. Gulf/Japan could ease to $18 short-term for want of grain orders.
Chicago grains futures were called lower by traders who said latest US Department of Agriculture estimates of the 1996 US harvest were about in line with or above average estimates.
The USDA saw China 1996/97 wheat imports at 7 million tonnes, down from 12 million the previous year.
Biffex futures also eased by 1200 GMT across-the-board where traded with most active October down 15 at 1,170, although in thin volume of 50 lots.
John Banaszkiewicz at CIS in a mid-week commentary said mixed opinion in the marketplace made direction hard to quantify.
"On one side we have the bears who see very little demand nearby, a glut of vessels open, no grain activity until late November, increased supply of new building etc".
The bears cited a premium out to $3.0 for November/December from prompt to suggest that bullishness was already factored in to forward rates.

But the CIS commentary added that on the other side "non grain demand especially coal on the upswing to restock furnaces, a big spike in grain shipments in Nov/Dec as new crop turns on the export valve, is causing the market to perceive we have hit the bottom..."

Coal fixtures included Merchant Pilot 50,000/10 tonnes Mobile/Eregli at $8.85 for 20-30 September to Margem and, for same dates, Bai De Arama 55,000/10 tonnes coal Roberts Bank/Genoa $9.45 to Deulimar.
China Steel fixed 1994-built Suma Newcastle/Kaohsiung 5-15 October at $4.90.
